newsitem.title: USA: Oil, grain prices rise ahead of holiday break.
newsitem.headline: Oil, grain prices rise ahead of holiday break.

text.p: Grain and oil prices closed mostly higher in light trading during abbreviated trading sessions Tuesday as markets closed early for Christmas.

At the Chicago Board of Trade grain prices were led higher by a strong speculative rally in soybeans. Soybeans opened lower but soon climbed on heavy buying by Refco Inc., a large professional trader, floor sources said.
January soybeans closed 7 cents higer at $7.07 a bushel.
"It probably was short covering before the holiday. There was no news and South American weather is still very good," said grain market analyst Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Short covering refers to buying of futures contracts to offset an existing earlier sale of futures, called a "short" position.

The rally ran counter to selling pressure Monday tied to good growing weather for Brazil, the No. 2 soybean exporter after the United States. Brazil has just planted its latest crop, expected to result in record production.
Wheat futures were buoyed by the soybean rally, again despite good weather in Argentina, a competing exporter.
March wheat closed 1-1/4 cents higher at $3.91-3/4 a bushel and March corn also rose, up 1/4 cent at $2.66-3/4.
At the New York Mercantile Exchange, energy prices rose in thin volume with strength in European prices setting the tone amid a lack of other market news.
"There is a lack of liquidity, but we were up in London," said Warren Tashnek, president of Fimat USA Futures.
February crude oil closed up 31 cents a barrel at $25.10 and January gasoline rose 0.66 cent a gallon at 69.56 cents.

Some weather forecasters predicted temperatures in the U.S. Northeast to drop below normal levels by late this week, and an overnight snowstorm in the upper Midwest may have also spurred some shortcovering in heating fuels, traders said.
January heating oil ended up 0.32 cent a gallon at 71.40 cents and February natural gas rose $0.008 at $3.705 per million British Thermal Units.
At the New York Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange, coffee prices ignored a buildup in cash coffee stocks to end higher. March coffee closed 1.65 cent higher at 114.75 cents a pound.

U.S. coffee stocks in certified delivery warehouses rose a strong 21,744 60-kg bags in the week ended December 20 to total 34,315 bags, as Latin American growers stepped up shipments to the United States.
Traders cited the rise in futures to the thin trading conditions ahead of the holiday break.
